newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan second-tier brokers may revise forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Japan second-tier brokers may revise forecasts.

text.p: Some of Japan's 10 second-tier securities houses are expected to revise their earnings forecasts for the first half of the 1996/97 fiscal year on September 19, industry sources said on Monday.
"It is not known how many second-tier brokers will revise their earnings, but there are several which are considering doing so," an industry source said.
Under the rules of the Tokyo Stock Exchange, a firm must revise its earnings forecast if its net or current profits are up or down 30 percent or more from its earlier earnings forecast.

All 10 brokers in May forecast parent current profits for the six months to the end of September, but this was based on an expected average turnover value on the stock exchange of around 400 billion yen to 450 billion yen a day.
While turnover value in the first three months of the fiscal year was above that, in July it was 318 billion yen and in August it was about 289 billion yen a day.
So far in September turnover is also still very low.
In 1995/96, out of the 10 second-tier brokers, only Kokusai Securities Co Ltd and Wako Securities Co Ltd posted parent current profits.
